lineage.Process: CalculateField Evacuation_Analysis_HQ30 I_swi "!HubDist! * (1 + float(!Local_SVI!))" "Python 3" # Text NO_ENFORCE_DOMAINS

dataIdInfo.idPurp: The purpose of this dataset is to quantify the "Evacuation Resistance" of residential populations under flood stress. By moving beyond simple Euclidean distance, this analysis identifies areas where the interplay between physical geography and social vulnerability creates high-risk bottlenecks. It is designed to assist emergency planners in locating optimal sites for new shelters and in assigning specialized mobile rescue units to zones where high "Evacuation Lag" is predicted.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
This analysis layer simulates the evacuation dynamics for residents within the HQ30 flood hazard extents. The primary innovation of this dataset is the integration of "Social Friction" into spatial distance metrics.

While HubDist provides the geometric baseline, the I_swi (Socially-Weighted Distance) corrects the misconception that physical proximity alone guarantees safety; it accounts for how lack of financial resources or administrative resilience increases the difficulty of traversing that distance. Furthermore, the HH_Vuln and L_delay metrics address the "Evacuation Lag" phenomenon—correcting the flawed assumption that households move as single, able-bodied units. Instead, these fields highlight that households with high dependency loads (children and elderly) face a significant time penalty during the "preparation phase" of evacuation. This spatial logic identifies "Hidden Isolation" zones: areas that appear close to safety on a map but are functionally stranded due to the complex caregiving and socio-economic burdens of the inhabitants.

enttyp.enttypd: Each entity represents a spatial feature(point)
enttyp.enttypds: Author-defined, based on analytical purpose and processing logic of this study, following ISO 19115 metadata guidance and ArcGIS Pro documentation standards.

attr.attrdef: Euclidean Distance to Safety: The linear distance (in meters) from each residential point (Origin) to the nearest designated shelter or safety hub (Destination).
Socially-Weighted Distance Index: A modified distance metric that adjusts the physical distance by the local social vulnerability, representing the "functional distance" a resident must overcome.
attr.attrdefs: HubDist*(1 + Local_SVI). Derived from the theory that social barriers act as physical friction during evacuation.

attr.attrdef: Household Dependency Load: A ratio quantifying the care burden within a household by calculating the density of children and elderly members per domestic unit.
attr.attrdefs: Formula: (Bevölke_1 + Bevölke_2) / Haushalte_. Defined as a proxy for family-level self-evacuation capacity.

attr.attrdef: Evacuation Lag (Care-induced Delay): An estimated delay factor that predicts the increase in time required to initiate evacuation due to household caregiving responsibilities.
attr.attrdefs: Formula: HubDist *HH_Vuln. Based on the rationale that caregivers must overcome mobility constraints before beginning travel.
